# DSH plugins directory

> Curated and install-checked directory of plugins for DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`), DeepSeek's open-source agent harness built on the bet that everything is a plugin. The curated page is organised by the job each plugin does; the generated catalog is the full resolvable set.

This repository ships a curated page for people and a set of generated layers for machines.
Everything under "Generated data" is rewritten in full by the `verify-installs` workflow, Mondays at
08:23 UTC and on manual dispatch. Editing those files by hand is pointless; they are overwritten.

## Files

- [README.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZeroPointRepo/awesome-dsh-plugins/main/README.md): the curated page. Entries grouped by what each plugin does for the reader, with a fenced install command each.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZeroPointRepo/awesome-dsh-plugins/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): the bar an entry has to clear and the exact format a new entry uses.

## Generated data

- [CATALOG.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZeroPointRepo/awesome-dsh-plugins/main/CATALOG.md): every plugin this repo can resolve and install-check, as a markdown table. Columns: plugin, what it does, stars, install command, verified mark.
- [catalog.csv](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZeroPointRepo/awesome-dsh-plugins/main/catalog.csv): the same rows as CSV. Header: `name,description,stars,install_command,verified,repo_url,screenshots`. `verified` is `true` or `false`; `screenshots` is semicolon separated and may be empty.
- [plugins.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZeroPointRepo/awesome-dsh-plugins/main/plugins.json): the same rows in the dsh-market registry schema, so a marketplace client can consume this file directly as a registry. Top level: `name, url, source, updated, count, categories, plugins`. Per entry: `name, owner, url, category, description.en, stars, install, added`, plus `screenshots` where they exist. The live entry count is the top level `count` field, which is why no count is written into this file.
- [badges/coverage.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZeroPointRepo/awesome-dsh-plugins/main/badges/coverage.json): shields.io endpoint schema. `message` carries both tiers as `N install-verified / M resolved`. The two numbers answer different questions and only the first is a claim about function; see "The two tiers" below.
- [badges/verified.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZeroPointRepo/awesome-dsh-plugins/main/badges/verified.json): shields.io endpoint schema. `message` carries the passing-over-checked ratio from the last run.
- [badges/checked-at.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZeroPointRepo/awesome-dsh-plugins/main/badges/checked-at.json): shields.io endpoint schema. `message` is the date of that run. Use it as the as-of date for everything above.
- [.github/data/first-seen.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZeroPointRepo/awesome-dsh-plugins/main/.github/data/first-seen.json): the date this list first carried each entry. Cumulative and never back-dated, so a re-listed entry keeps its original date. It records when we listed a plugin, not when the plugin was created.
- [mcp-configs/](https://github.com/ZeroPointRepo/awesome-dsh-plugins/tree/main/mcp-configs): ready-to-download MCP config files for entries installed that way rather than through `dsh plugin add`.

## The two tiers

This directory publishes two counts and they are not interchangeable.

- **resolved** is the size of CATALOG.md: every plugin the generator could reach through the
  GitHub API and index. Reaching a repository means it exists, answers, and is not archived.
  **It is not evidence that the plugin installs or that it works.** A resolved entry with no
  install command is still resolved.
- **install-verified** is the smaller number: entries on the curated page whose install command
  was re-checked against the project's own source on the last run, per the rules below.

Read `install-verified` as the number this directory stands behind and `resolved` as the size of
the index. Anything that treats a resolved entry as a working one is over-reading the data. Both
numbers are generated by the weekly run; neither is typed by a person.

## What the verified mark means

- `✅` in CATALOG.md and `verified: true` in the CSV mean one specific thing: on the last run, the
  install command's package spec was still present in the linked project's own README, the repo
  resolved through the GitHub API, and any npm pin still matched the registry's current release.
- `—` and `verified: false` mean that check did not pass or does not apply. It is not a claim that
  the plugin is broken. Entries installed from a downloaded MCP config rather than a package spec
  land here by construction.
- The check catches three things a link checker structurally cannot see: a renamed repo, an archived
  repo, and command drift, because all three still return HTTP 200.
- Both badge files are written by the run. Neither is a hand-set claim, and neither number appears
  anywhere else as prose.
- If more than 5% of README reads fail in a run, the generator keeps the existing catalog rather
  than publish false unverified marks. A stale catalog is preferred over a wrong one.
- This is a curated list, not a security audit. A verified mark says the install command works and
  the project is real, not that its code has been reviewed.

## How an agent should use this list

1. For the complete machine-readable set in one request, fetch `plugins.json`. For tabular work or
   citation, fetch `catalog.csv`. Both are single files and neither is paginated.
2. For a recommendation to a person, read `README.md`. It is grouped by task and it is the only
   layer where entries are curated rather than merely resolvable.
3. Read `badges/checked-at.json` and report that date alongside any claim taken from here.
4. Take install commands verbatim from the `install` field or the fenced block. Do not rebuild one
   from a repository URL, and do not drop or invent a version pin.
5. Carry the verified mark through to the person. Do not present `verified: false` as broken, and do
   not present `verified: true` as a safety endorsement.
6. Ask the person before installing a plugin or handing it credentials.
7. To add or correct an entry, open a pull request against `README.md`. The generated layers are
   rebuilt from it, so a change made in them is discarded. There is no write API and nothing here
   accepts a direct push.
